title: orch-respawn-reresolve AC1: unexplained 'invocations.length 1 instead of 2' with result.error undefined (root cause open)
description:
Surfaced during CAM-448 (US-R1-001 / US-R2-001) and deliberately left OPEN by that cycle rather than silently mitigated.

SYMPTOM (measured, twice): test/integration/orch-respawn-reresolve.test.ts, the AC1 END-TO-END RE-RESOLUTION test, failed under two separate full `bun run check:all` invocations with `invocations.length` of 1 instead of 2, while `result.error` was UNDEFINED. The same file and the same full suite were 100% green when run standalone.

WHY THIS IS NOT A TIMEOUT, and why the first mitigation was wrong: result.error undefined means no timeout fired at all. The real-subprocess wrapper exited cleanly after ONE claude invocation instead of two. US-R1-001 initially misdiagnosed this as the CAM-201 per-test-timeout flake class and raised only bun's OUTER per-test budget; the CAM-448 round-2 reviewer proved that could not address the recorded symptom, since node:child_process.spawnSync blocks the JS thread in a native waitpid-style loop and no JS timer can preempt it mid-call. US-R2-001 corrected the theory in patterns.md, raised the binding INNER spawnSync budget (15s->25s, outer 20s->30s as margin), and added result.status/result.signal/result.stdout/result.stderr to both assertions' failure messages so a recurrence is diagnosable from test output alone.

WHAT WAS RULED OUT (bounded empirical stress testing by US-R2-001, all NEGATIVE, i.e. did not reproduce): 20-70 concurrent CPU-bound background processes; sequential and parallel repeated `bun test` runs of the isolated file; one full `bun run check:all` whose test/coverage/skip-ratchet gates each execute the entire suite sequentially.

WHAT REMAINS UNKNOWN: why the orchestrator wrapper would exit cleanly after a single claude invocation instead of respawning. That is either a genuine non-determinism in the respawn path under contention (which would be a PRODUCT defect, not a test defect) or an unidentified test-harness race. Nothing currently distinguishes the two.

WHY IT MATTERS: if it is the product path, this is the respawn/re-resolution mechanism that CAM-425 shipped and that the orchestrator self-handoff (CAM-23) depends on, so a silent single-invocation exit would mean a failed respawn in production, not just a flaky test.

SIBLING: CAM-446 tracks the same family (orch-recycle-watch.test.ts non-determinism under CPU contention). Consider whether the two share a root cause before fixing either in isolation.

NEXT STEP: this issue exists to make the next recurrence actionable, since the diagnostic payload is now in place. Do not close it by raising a timeout. Either reproduce it with the new diagnostics and fix the real cause, or demonstrate it is a harness artifact with evidence.

SPEC NOTE: born stage:idea deliberately; it needs a /cam-spec pass with real oracle forms before it can be planned (ADR-0051).
